newsitem.title: INDIA: India's HZL to close unviable zinc mine
newsitem.headline: India's HZL to close unviable zinc mine

text.p: India's Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) has decided to close down its tungsten zinc ore mines at Nagaur in northern Rajasthan state as exploration had become unviable, a senior company official said on Monday.
"We have decided to close it because of less metal content," the official, who did not want to be identified, told Reuters by telephone from the company's headquarters in Udaipur.
He said exploration had become unviable because of higher mining costs.
"There is miserably less metal content in its ore. It goes down to 0.4-0.2 percent in some places," said the official.
He said HZL had decided to close it at the behest of the Ministry of Mines.
The official said about 140 workers in the mines have been offered voluntary retirement scheme.
HZL had acquired the mine from the Rajasthan State Tungsten Development Corporation.
HZL has an installed capacity of 152,000 tonnes of zinc. Its Rampura-Agucha mines with a metal content of 12.5 percent in ore ranks among one of the best in the world.
